the study of the convergence of wages among the Portuguese and Spanish borderland NUTs 2 regions.
the study of regional income differences in the borderland, with the use of the convergence theory and the spatial econometric methods.
the analysis of the regional inequalities in the borderland and the spatial autocorrelation of the wages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a spatial pattern in the wages of the borderland regions of Portugal and of Spain.
the borderland is not a place where regional inequalities are less important than in other parts of Europe.
the regional income differences are not converging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial autocorrelation is a relevant issue in the study of regional income differences.
the borderland regions of Portugal and the Spanish regions located in the border with Portugal are not converging in terms of per capita wages.
wages in the Portuguese borderland are lower than in the Spanish one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the borderland regions are not converging to each other and that the spatial correlation of wages is positive, that is, regions with high wages have neighbours with high wages.
the spatial autocorrelation of wages in the borderland is not only positive but also significant.
wages are not only spatially correlated, but they are also converging, which means that the differences between wages are diminishing over time.
